correctness.rationale: Exact 24-vertex, 14-facet, 36-edge enumeration gives all generic central intersection vertices. Only three vertex-sign walls divide an ordered positive normal chamber into five connected cones. Exact integer witnesses determine side count on each region, and solid-angle formulas prove the full probability law; verified by a standalone 3,911-check independent-incidence program and exact chamber arguments. Finite grid and floating-point angle checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The motivating March 2026 truncated-octahedral BCC Voronoi study establishes isoperimetric optimization and cell geometry rather than Haar section-complexity probabilities. Five exact normal chambers, the six/eight/ten-side law, and their solid-angle weights are not logical corollaries of the compared cell-area or unrelated-polytope random-slicing theorems. Targeted semantic and primary-source searches did not recover this distribution; historical priority remains genuinely uncertain.

value.rationale: The BCC Voronoi truncated octahedron is a canonical space-filling polyhedron, and its full three-valued central-section complexity distribution and five-cone angular classification give a motivated, reproducible geometric tomography benchmark. Unlike familiar vertex or face totals, the result requires nontrivial direction-space partition and exact spherical area evaluation and is not a mere numerical experiment.
